text: On the Machamer-Darden-Craver (MDC) account, a mechanism consists of:
choices: Laws from which the phenomenon is deductively derived (the covering-law model)
Bridge laws connecting the vocabularies of two theories
A single localized brain region responsible for the whole function
Entities and activities, organized spatially and temporally, that produce the phenomenon
explanation: On the MDC account a mechanism is a set of entities and activities, organized spatially and temporally, that produce the phenomenon to be explained. Deriving the phenomenon from laws is the rival covering-law model; bridge laws belong to Nagelian reduction; and a single localized region is neither necessary nor what 'mechanism' means.
